definitions.explanation: A celebratory gathering with food and drink. Has an elegant, literary tone compared to the everyday word パーティー. Often used for formal or traditional celebrations.

examples.japanese: {盛大|せいだい}な{宴|うたげ}が{開|ひら}かれた。
{勝利|しょうり}を{祝|いわ}う{宴|うたげ}は{夜|よる}{遅|おそ}くまで{続|つづ}いた。
examples.english: The celebration of the victory continued until late at night.

examples.japanese: {城|しろ}の{大広間|おおひろま}で{華|はな}やかな{宴|うたげ}が{催|もよお}され、{家臣|かしん}たちが{集|あつ}まった。
examples.english: A splendid banquet was held in the great hall of the castle, and the retainers gathered.

notes:
USAGE:
A literary and elegant word. In modern Japanese, it is used in formal writing, historical narratives, and creative works more than in casual conversation. For everyday parties and gatherings, パーティー or {飲|の}み{会|かい} are more natural.

SIMILAR WORDS:
{宴会|えんかい} is the more common compound for a banquet or dinner party and is used in everyday contexts ({忘年会|ぼうねんかい}, {歓迎会|かんげいかい}, etc.). {宴|うたげ} has a more poetic and literary feel.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {宴|うたげ}を{開|ひら}く: to hold a feast
- {宴|うたげ}を{催|もよお}す: to host a banquet
- {盛大|せいだい}な{宴|うたげ}: a grand feast
- {宴|うたげ}の{席|せき}: the banquet table/occasion
